tables.description: Descriptive statistics (mean, percentiles, std) for ISSUE, DT-ISSUE, BM, ME, MOM and the contemporaneous 1-year return, 1970-2003.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct variable construction on the post-1970 sample: split-adjusted shares via the CRSP cumulative adjustment factor (eqs 1-2), annual and 5-year logged issuance, Compustat data60 book-to-market with December ME denominator, log market equity, and 6-month momentum — plus that the CRSP universe and nonmissing-return / 6-month-listing filters reproduce the paper's ~2.29-2.31M firm-month observation counts.
tables.paper_quote: Panel A: Simple Statistics. ... The sample observations range between 2,285,189 observations (for $MOM$ ) and 2,312,597 observations (for $ISSUE_{-11,0}$ ). (L156)
tables.notes: Zero-valued percentile cells (issue p25/median, dt_issue p25/median, bm p75) carry tolerance 100%: relative tolerance is undefined at a paper value of 0, so they pass when our value rounds to 0.00 at 2 decimals. The paper says Table I variables are 'measured at the end of December' (L156), but the reported observation counts (2.29-2.31M) only reconcile with the full monthly panel over 1970-2003 (~5,600 firms/month), not 34 December cross-sections; statistics are therefore computed on the pooled monthly panel. This interpretation is logged in assumptions.md.

tables.table_ref: Table III, Panels A and B
tables.description: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions of 1-month (Panel A) and 6-month (Panel B) stock returns on BM, BM Dum, ME, MOM, ISSUE, DT-ISSUE and DT-Dum, January 1970 to December 2003, 396 months, 2,155,945 firm-observations.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the paper's headline methodology end-to-end: the 6-month-lagged ISSUE_{-17,-6} and DT-ISSUE_{-65,-6} predictors (eqs 2-3 with the DT dummy), the horse-race specification design (5 univariate rows, controls row, issuance-pair row, full row), monthly Fama-MacBeth averaging with adjusted R-squared reporting, 1% winsorization of all right-hand-side variables, the x100 (percent) scaling of regression dependent returns, and Pontiff (1996) overlap-consistent t-statistics for the 6-month panel. Reproducing the ISSUE slope of -2.23 (t = -7.08) and DT-ISSUE slope of -0.71 validates share-issuance construction, timing conventions, and the regression machinery simultaneously.
tables.paper_quote: These regressions are for the 396 months from January 1970 to December 2003, with a total of 2,155,945 firm-observations. (L1074)
tables.notes: Panels A (1-month, all 8 specification rows) and B (6-month, rows 1-5) are fully legible in the OCR and committed cell-by-cell. Panel B rows 6-8 appear on the page-13 continuation (intercepts 8.80/8.81; ISSUE slope approx -10.92, t approx -6.89) but panel attribution of the page-14 continuation (Panels C-E: 1-year, 2nd-year, 3rd-year returns) is ambiguous under OCR, so those panels are evaluated at pattern level against the paper's narrative (L2105-2125): ISSUE remains negative and strongly significant at all holding periods, BM t-stats increase with horizon, MOM t-stat peaks at 6 months. Tables II and IV are excluded from scope: they require Thomson SDC Platinum SEO/repurchase/merger event data (L341, L2168), unavailable in ClickHouse. Regression dependent variables are in percent (intercepts ~0.8-2.7 vs ~1% mean monthly return), documented in assumptions.md.

tables.table_ref: Table III, Panels C, D and E
tables.description: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions of 1-year (Panel C), 2nd-year (Panel D) and 3rd-year (Panel E) stock returns on BM, BM Dum, ME, MOM, ISSUE, DT-ISSUE and DT-Dum, January 1970 to December 2003 (408 in-sample months). Long-horizon extension of Table III Panels A/B.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the paper's horizon-stability claim (content.md L31: 'Our results remain strong for holding periods ranging from one month to 3 years'): ISSUE remains the most significant predictor at the 1/2/3-year horizons with overlap-consistent AR(11/23/35) t-stats, and DT-ISSUE loses significance in the 2- and 3-year joint specs (L2128). Exercises the same horse-race machinery as T3 on the r12/r24_y2/r36_y3 holding-period return columns (EWRETD-imputed per A7 for the year-2 and year-3 windows).
tables.paper_quote: The longer holding period results are broadly consistent with the 1-month results. The signs of the slopes remain unchanged... Regardless of holding period, the t-statistics on both issuance measures remain stable and strongly significant. The t-statistics on annual issuance are stronger than the t-statistics on BE, ME, and MOM for all holding periods. ... Although in the joint regressions 5-year issuance is significant for holding periods up to 1 year, it loses significance in the 2- and 3-year return joint regressions. (L2128)
tables.notes: All 198 coefficient/t-stat/R2 cells of Panels C (1-year, k=12, AR(11)), D (2nd-year, k=24, AR(23)) and E (3rd-year, k=36, AR(35)) are legible in the OCR: Panel C at content.md L1501-1695, Panel D at L1698-1892, Panel E rows 1 at L1895-1935 and rows 2-8 on the page-14 continuation at L1952-2122. No cells were skipped for legibility. Dependent returns r12/r24_y2/r36_y3 are x100 (A3); year-2 (t+12..t+23) and year-3 (t+24..t+35) windows are EWRETD-imputed (A7). DT_DUM_FLIP=True (A19 ratified) is applied, so only intercept and DT-Dum-own-coefficient differ from the as-built polarity; ISSUE and DT-ISSUE are polarity-invariant. KNOWN DEVIATION: under the ratified flipped polarity the Panel E DT-Dum coefficient cells (pE_r6/r7/r8_dt_dum) come out NEGATIVE while the paper prints POSITIVE (+1.98/+2.21/+3.12) — the mirror image of the A15 finding (Panels A-D require the flipped sign; Panel E's printed DT-Dum sign matches the as-built polarity). This is a paper-side DT-Dum polarity inconsistency at the 3-year horizon; it is the ONLY sign deviation (3 FAIL cells) and does not touch any ratified convention or the issuance coefficients. Tolerances: +/-40% for coefficients and t-stats, +/-25% for R2, matching the T3 contract.

tables.description: Descriptive statistics for ISSUE, DT-ISSUE, BM, ME, MOM and the contemporaneous 1-year return over the out-of-sample September 1932 to December 1969 period.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the split-adjusted share-issuance construction extends correctly to pre-1970 CRSP (where issuance is far rarer: mean 0.01 vs 0.04, std 0.07 vs 0.15, 62.6% zero vs 24.2%), validating the cumulative-factor adjustment across the 1930s-1960s split history and the out-of-sample universe composition (~524-528K firm-months). Matching these frequencies is a sharp test of the shares-outstanding pipeline independent of any regression.
tables.paper_quote: The sample observations range between 524,260 observations (for $MOM$ ) and 528,200 observations (for $R_{-11,0}$ ). (L2263)
tables.notes: BM cells (oos_bm_mean, oos_bm_std) depend on the Davis-Fama-French (2000) pre-1970 book-equity file the authors obtained from Ken French (L2445), not Compustat; if that file is absent from ClickHouse these cells are evaluated as SKIP and the BM-dependent rows of Table VI are reported at pattern level. The zero 75th percentile of pre-1970 annual issuance (62.6% of firms never change shares) carries tolerance 100%: it passes when our value rounds to 0.00.

tables.description: Out-of-sample Fama-MacBeth regressions of 1-month stock returns on BM, BM Dum, ME, MOM, ISSUE, DT-ISSUE and DT-Dum, September 1932 to December 1969, 444 months, 373,590 firm-observations.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the full methodology (share-issuance construction, FM machinery, overlap t-stats) behaves correctly OUT of sample: the paper's key out-of-sample finding is that annual issuance does NOT predict monthly returns pre-1970 (Panel A ISSUE slopes 0.52, 0.27, 0.84 — all positive and insignificant, t < 1 — vs post-1970 -2.23, t = -7.08), while ME stays significantly negative and MOM stays positive but insignificant. Reproducing both the sign flip of the ISSUE slope and its loss of significance is the paper's central pre-1970 claim and a strong guard against overfitting the post-1970 pipeline.
tables.paper_quote: These regressions are for the 444 months from September 1932 (to ensure the existence of shares outstanding) to December 1969, with a total of 373,590 firm-observations. (L2463)
tables.notes: Panels B-E of Table VI (6-month through 3rd-year returns) sit in the OCR-degraded page-20/21 continuations with uncertain panel attribution; they are evaluated at pattern level against the paper's narrative (L3295-3310): of 40 specifications, annual issuance is negative and significant in exactly one (annual-return joint regression), DT-ISSUE is significant-positive in 2 of 40 and insignificant in 38, ME is significantly negative in all, MOM is positive in all but its 1-month slopes are insignificant. ISSUE-related cells carry 100% tolerance because the paper's claim about them is sign-and-significance (positive, |t| < 1), not magnitude — matching the pattern (positive slope, t far below 2) is the target. BM rows depend on DFF (2000) book equity (see T5 notes).
